PACKAGES

Test design batch 5 is committed and red for the stated reasons, but the designer returned one open package (DP-8) that the engineer's work depends on. No engineer or reviewer was started.

## Branch
- `w1/W1-11`, head `39a574c6`, clean tree.
- `c3072357`: merge of `w1/integrate` (`9ab23f3c`), with `Task: DAEO-be7u` and `Role: orchestrator`. No file under `tests/acceptance/` was changed on both sides (14 files on ours, 37 on theirs, none shared). Containment flagged the merge; that is a record (DEC-254).
- `39a574c6`: tests batch 5, by a fresh designer started with `gov launch`. 95 → 132 cases, 37 added after implementation.

## Package DP-8: how the checker learns whether the dropped parent changed the decision
- **Question.** When a merge keeps one parent's changed file whole, the helper lists the path as `brought` whether the other parent left the decision alone or changed it too. The first is ordinary integration and must pass. The second (a concurrent demotion, the owner's file over an agent's, a moved file over a demotion at the old path) must fail. From `own` and `brought` alone the two cannot be told apart, and the "more than one parent changed it" rule (DEC-410 DP-24) holds only under `tests/acceptance/**`.
- **Why now.** The engineer builds the rule next, and "only through the helper" leaves no stated way to read the decision's state at the merge base. Five cases turn on it: three green that must stay green, two red.
- **Options.**
  - (a) The checker asks git for the merge base itself, only for a parent pair where the helper listed the path as `brought` (so exactly one base exists), and reads the decision there by `id`.
  - (b) The helper exposes what it already computes: the base per parent, or the paths more than one parent changed. This changes W1-50's interface before its merge.
  - (c) The checker keeps its own ancestry rule for these merges. That is a second merge reader, and the one the three reviewed histories defeat.
- **Impact.** Under (a) two places name a merge base, but they cannot disagree where the helper fails closed. Under (b) there is one strict reading, at the cost of changing a helper that has had seven review rounds. Under (c) the holes stay.
- **Reversibility.** High for (a) and (b); the cases assert only the checker's result and stand under either.
- **Cost.** About 10 lines in the checker for (a); about 10 in the helper plus its cases for (b); none for (c).
- **Recommendation.** (a); the designer recommends the same. Confidence: medium, because neither the designer nor I have seen the helper's code, only its description.
- **Who decides.** (b) touches containment's helper, which DEC-416 excludes from delegation. (a) adds a git call in the checker only.

## To confirm: what DP-6 option (b) says
The designer could not see the DP-6 package the owner answered. The README's older DP-6 text has an option (b) that reads the other way on a concurrent demotion. The cases follow DEC-398's words and the rule in my brief: an agent's merge that keeps `ACTIVE` over a concurrent owner demotion fails. If the owner's option (b) meant otherwise, the cases to revise are `test_an_agent_merge_that_keeps_active_over_a_concurrent_owner_demotion_fails` (2 cases) and `test_an_agent_merge_that_keeps_the_owner_file_over_an_agent_file_at_the_same_path_fails`.

## What the designer settled
- **A moved decision file at a merge.** The decision is its `id`, so a side that only moves the file changed neither id, status nor presence. The side that demoted or removed it at the old path changed it. A merge that holds the moved file `ACTIVE` is therefore the change, and the finding names the id and the new path.
- **The false alarms are findings**, stated in the README, and the same merges with `Role: owner` pass. DEC-398, DEC-403 and DEC-410 (DP-23) say fail closed, and no decision excepts decision files.
  - The designer added a fourth, plainer shape: the owner approves on one of two crossed lines and an agent's ordinary merge brings it across. It is the one fail-closed case that is red today.
  - A control keeps a criss-cross green where every parent holds the same approved file.
- **`MergeReadError`.** One case reaches it through a 25-parent merge and accepts a finding or a `GovError`, never a pass. It is green today and pins the behaviour for after the repair.

## Red check (run by me)
W1-11: **13 failed, 119 passed**. All 13 fail on behaviour assertions; none fails on an import of the absent helper, and there is no collection error.

| Red | Reason | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `no ACTIVE_UNAPPROVED finding names ...`, findings none | old branch merged into the demoted line (2); moved file over a demotion at the old path (2); a second merge hides an agent's re-activation; criss-cross with the approval on one line; replace ref |
| 5 | `no FRONTMATTER_UNREADABLE finding names the file ...` | byte-order mark, blank line, `--- # c`, CR-only, UTF-16 |
| 1 | `no finding names the file docs/adr/ADR-0011.md` | `type: decision` without `id` |

- The 24 new green cases are controls (owner merges, ordinary integration, the crossed lines that both hold the approved file) and pins the checker already flags: the two concurrent demotions, the owner's file over an agent's, three fail-closed shapes, and the 25-parent merge.
- The 95 earlier cases pass, with no assertion or fixture changed. Revisions to existing files:
  - `test_w1_11_approval_merges.py`: docstring only (owner decision: DEC-398).
  - `test_w1_11_unreadable.py`: docstring, and 5 parameters added to the existing function (DEC-387).
  - `w1_11_support.py`: extended with defaults.
- Interface change: none.

  - **W1-46** live sessions: 23 setup errors (470 passed). The file alone: 36 passed. The previous lead saw the same.

## What the engineer needs
Start after W1-50's branch is merged into `w1/integrate` and DP-8 is answered. The work is in `src/gov/decisions/checker.py`.
- Read merges only through `gov.guard.containment_merge.read_merge`; the checker's own ancestry walk goes.
- A merge that holds a decision `ACTIVE` sets nothing only when all three hold; otherwise the merge's own `Role` trailer is the fact:
  - a parent holds it `ACTIVE`;
  - no other parent changed its id, status or presence since the merge base;
  - every `ACTIVE` parent's setting commits carry the owner's fact.
- Follow the decision by `id` across a move when comparing parents with the base.
- With several merge bases or none, fail closed, but pass where every parent holds the same file.
- Turn `MergeReadError` into a finding or a `GovError`.
- Report the five unreadable heads as `FRONTMATTER_UNREADABLE`, leaving CRLF files and prose unreported.
- Fail a `type: decision` file without `id`.
- Run git with replace refs off.
- If the helper's interface changes before its merge, a designer revises the cases ("owner decision: early test design").

## Learning metrics so far
- KPI disputes: none this round.
- Acceptance tests rewritten after implementation: 0 assertions; 2 docstrings and 5 added parameters, as listed above.
- Tests added after implementation: 37 this batch (67 → 82 → 95 → 132 overall).
- LOC: `checker.py` is 360 lines against an estimate of 310. I estimate the repair at 80 to 120 changed lines with small net growth.
- Engineer iterations: converged.
- Review to repair: the one remaining review is the one DEC-398 grants; a fail-open that survives it is a package to the owner.
- False findings: none.

## Records
- Containment attributed the designer's files and commit to my waiting Bash call (DEC-254).
- The designer reported running one Bash command with a here-document; it printed one line and wrote nothing.
- Not yet done by anyone, for the reviewer's brief: a replay of the approval rule over this repository's own history, and the timing probe on many `ACTIVE` decisions under a long history.
- Residuals the designer recorded in the README, none fail-open:
  - the owner set `ACTIVE` on both sides of a merge with one merge base;
  - an owner's merge where an `ACTIVE` parent was set by an agent;
  - a merge with more than 24 parents that touches no decision;
  - crossed or unrelated merges deep in history rather than at `HEAD`.

The lead checkpoint in the worktree (`.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/CHECKPOINT.md`) is updated for the next lead. Nothing is running, and nothing else on this ticket can proceed until the helper's branch is merged and DP-8 is answered.
